name: Edit a video
about: You have footage of a long-form video (16:9). The agent cuts the rough, you approve and lock the talk, it dresses it with overlays (no captions: those are only for Shorts), checks it, and you export.

card.bring: A recording of a long video (16:9), or several.
card.you: Tell the agent what you want, watch the rough cut and keep or restore its cuts, approve, check the final, export.
card.agent: Cuts the dead air and retakes, adds overlays, zooms and captions, then checks its own work.

start.hint: Next: drop your recordings into the media bin, then press Go.

withFootage.hint: Next: your footage is going in. When it is there, press Go and the agent asks what you want from the edit.

stages.title: Brief
stages.focus: This is a long-form edit (1920x1080). Ask about the length they want, what must stay, what can go, and the look of the overlays (no captions on a long video; the house rules already say what the user wants about them: do not ask again what they answered there).

stages.title: Rough cut
stages.focus: Make the rough cut from the footage in video/footage. In order: transcribe each recording once (transcribe.py, verbatim and aligned), scan.py, write video/out/edl.json with a cut_before on every cut (flag the judgment calls with an ask), joins.py check then snap until no word is clipped, build_rough.py, then handover.py (rough.json, rough-words.json, cuts.json with Before/After clips). Transcription, the build and the handover run in the background. Report the length before and after and the cuts by kind.

stages.title: Rough review
stages.focus: The user watches the rough and goes through the Cuts list (Keep / Restore / Note). Approve & lock hashes edl.json and rough.mp4: the talk is fixed from here.

stages.title: Visuals
stages.focus: Dress the locked rough: first write video/out/visual-plan.md (visuals-plan skill: each beat, what is on screen where, the one visual that helps), then write video/out/events.json (overlays, zooms, sounds; never captions on a long video, only the kinds the house rules allow) with the Events builder, times only from rough-words.json, then run.py --proof for a cheap look, fix what is off, and run.py --final (in the background). Never touch edl.json or rough.mp4. Report the overlays by kind and the render times.

stages.title: Inspect
stages.focus: Run check_cut.py (length, frames, locked files, voice) and look at video/out/frames.jpg. Check there are no captions (a long video never has them), that no overlay covers what the screen is showing, that the pace has no long stretch with nothing changing, and each overlay against video/out/visual-plan.md: does it point at, explain, count or compare something real? Any emoji, any lone text (a word or line on its own, not part of a callout, diagram, scoreboard or list), echo text or the same move repeated is a finding.

stages.title: Final review
stages.focus: The user watches final.mp4. Sending it back goes to Visuals: the talk stays locked.

stages.title: Export
stages.focus: MP4, an SRT subtitle file (for YouTube, never burned in), FCPXML and OTIO from the Export tab.
